## Functions

```{r}
`%notin%` <- Negate(`%in%`)

clean.labels <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    gsub("'", "", .) %>%
    gsub("\"", "", .) %>%
    gsub("%", "percent", .) %>%
    gsub("^[ ]+", "", .) %>%
    make.names(.) %>%
    gsub("[.]+", "_", .) %>%
    gsub("[_]+", "_", .) %>%
    tolower(.) %>%
    gsub("_$", "", .)
}

# Calculate a pairwise association between all variables in a data-frame. In particular nominal vs
# nominal with Chi-square, numeric vs numeric with Pearson correlation, and nominal vs numeric with
# ANOVA. Adopted from https://stackoverflow.com/a/52557631/590437
mixed_assoc <- function(df, cor_method = "spearman", adjust_cramersv_bias = TRUE) {
  df_comb <- expand.grid(names(df), names(df), stringsAsFactors = F) %>% set_names("X1", "X2")

  is_nominal <- function(x) class(x) %in% c("factor", "character")
  is_numeric <- function(x) { is.integer(x) || is_double(x) }

  f <- function(xName, yName) {
    x <- pull(df, xName)
    y <- pull(df, yName)

    result <- if (is_nominal(x) && is_nominal(y)) {
      cv <- cramerV(as.character(x), as.character(y), bias.correct = adjust_cramersv_bias)
      data.frame(xName, yName, assoc = cv, type = "cramersV")
    } else if (is_numeric(x) && is_numeric(y)) {
      correlation <- cor(x, y, method = cor_method, use = "complete.obs")
      data.frame(xName, yName, assoc = correlation, type = "correlation")
    } else if (is_numeric(x) && is_nominal(y)) {
      r_squared <- summary(lm(x ~ y))$r.squared
      data.frame(xName, yName, assoc = sqrt(r_squared), type = "anova")
    } else if (is_nominal(x) && is_numeric(y)) {
      r_squared <- summary(lm(y ~ x))$r.squared
      data.frame(xName, yName, assoc = sqrt(r_squared), type = "anova")
    } else {
      warning(paste("unmatched column type combination: ", class(x), class(y)))
    }

    result %>%
      mutate(complete_obs_pairs = sum(!is.na(x) & !is.na(y)),
             complete_obs_ratio = complete_obs_pairs / length(x)) %>%
      rename(x = xName, y = yName)
  }

  map2_df(df_comb$X1, df_comb$X2, f)
}
```

## Data

### Load data

```{r}
filtered.raw <- readRDS("filtered.RDS")

# TODO convert Visual_details (col 58) into meaningful categories
cols_to_use <- c(1,4,5,8,10,12,
                  15,16,18:50,52:57,59,60)

filtered.data <- filtered.raw %>%
  select(all_of(cols_to_use)) %>%
  mutate(education = case_when(Educational_level == "University degree" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         is_transition = case_when(isTransition == "Transition" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         task = case_when(str_detect(Task, ">") ~ "Waiting", T ~ Task),
         male = case_when(Gender == "Male" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         right_handed = case_when(Handedness == "Right handed" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         task = clean.labels(task)) %>%
  select(-Task, -Educational_level, -Gender, -Gender_identity, -Age_Group, -isTransition, -Handedness) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, factor) %>%
  filter(task == "training")

clean.raw <- readRDS("clean.RDS")
clean.data <- clean.raw %>%
  select(all_of(cols_to_use)) %>%
  mutate(education = case_when(Educational_level == "University degree" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         is_transition = case_when(isTransition == "Transition" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         task = case_when(str_detect(Task, ">") ~ "Waiting", T ~ Task),
         male = case_when(Gender == "Male" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         right_handed = case_when(Handedness == "Right handed" ~ 1, T ~ 0),
         task = clean.labels(task)) %>%
  select(-Task, -Educational_level, -Gender, -Gender_identity, -Age_Group, -isTransition, -Handedness) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, factor) %>%
  filter(task == "training") %>%
  na.omit()
```

### Data inspection

```{r}
mydata.cor <- cor(clean.data %>% select_if(is.numeric))
corrplot::corrplot(mydata.cor, order = "hclust", diag = T, tl.cex = 0.75)

reduced.data <- clean.data %>%
  select(
    # Correlated with average duration
    -maximum_fixation_duration, -maximum_saccadic_duration, -max_blink_duration,
    # Snellen right correlated with left but left has less correlation with age
    -snellen_right,
    # Walking and physical are similar
    -walking,
    # L/R mean/Max highly correlated, use l_mean with lowest correlation to other variables
    -r_max, -r_mean, -l_max,
    # entropy, GTE; STE somewhat correlated but GTE/STE has same correlation structure
    -ste,
    # mean saccadic/fixation count highly correlated, use fixations
    -mean_saccadic_count,
    # counts correlated strongly with duration, only keep time
    -blink_count, -saccadic_count, -fixation_count,
    # L/R entropy/variation is highly correlated, use r_variation because is most different
    -l_entropy, -r_entropy, -l_variation,
    # aid strength l/r highly correlated, keep left as snellen kept right
    -aid_strength_left,
    # depression, anxiety, stress are highly correlated, keep depression for correlation with others
    -anxiety, -stress
  )

mydata.cor <- cor(reduced.data %>% select_if(is.numeric))
corrplot::corrplot(mydata.cor, order = "hclust", diag = T, tl.cex = 0.75)
```

)

  filtered.data,

## Recipes

```{r}
reduced.recipe <-
  recipes::recipe(mo_ca ~ ., data = training(reduced.split)) %>%
  update_role(participant, new_role = "id") %>%
  recipes::step_string2factor(all_nominal()) %>%
  recipes::step_other(all_nominal(), threshold = 0.001) %>%
  recipes::step_nzv(all_nominal()) %>%
  prep()

reduced.formula <- formula(reduced.recipe)

filtered.recipe <-
  recipes::recipe(mo_ca ~ ., data = training(filtered.split)) %>%
  update_role(participant, new_role = "id") %>%
  recipes::step_string2factor(all_nominal()) %>%
  recipes::step_other(all_nominal(), threshold = 0.001) %>%
  recipes::step_nzv(all_nominal()) %>%
  prep()

filtered.formula <- formula(filtered.recipe)

clean.recipe <-
  recipes::recipe(mo_ca ~ ., data = training(clean.split)) %>%
  recipes::step_string2factor(all_nominal()) %>%
  recipes::step_other(all_nominal(), threshold = 0.01) %>%
  recipes::step_nzv(all_nominal()) %>%
  prep()
```

> Note: `mo_ca` is used as the outcome consistently across all three recipes/splits (the previous
> version mixed `performance_log` into the `reduced` recipe while everything downstream evaluated
> against `mo_ca` — that mismatch has been removed).

## Boruta feature selection

Boruta is run on the `filtered` pipeline; the resulting feature set (`boruta_features` /
`boruta_formula`) is what all "Boruta" model variants below are trained and tested on.

```{r}
feature_selection <- bake(filtered.recipe, new_data = training(filtered.split)) %>%
  select(-participant) # Remove ID column

# --- CHANGED: tighten Boruta's significance threshold (default pValue = 0.01) so it's harder
# for a feature to be classified Confirmed, with more maxRuns so stricter thresholds still reach
# a stable decision instead of leaving more features stuck Tentative.
boruta_p_value <- 0.005
boruta_max_runs <- 200

boruta_output <- Boruta(mo_ca ~ ., data = feature_selection,
                         pValue = boruta_p_value, maxRuns = boruta_max_runs, doTrace = 2)
# --- END CHANGED

# Resolve any 'Tentative' calls
final_boruta <- TentativeRoughFix(boruta_output)

table(final_boruta$finalDecision) # --- CHANGED: Confirmed/Rejected counts, to see the pValue effect

plot(final_boruta, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, main = "Boruta Feature Importance (all tested)")

# instead of keeping every Confirmed feature, rank them by importance and
# keep only the top N. Adjust top_n_features to control how aggressive the cut is.
top_n_features <- 15

boruta_importance <- Boruta::attStats(final_boruta) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
  dplyr::filter(decision == "Confirmed") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(medianImp))

# --- CHANGED: keep every Confirmed feature, no top-N cut
boruta_features <- boruta_importance %>%
  dplyr::pull(feature)
#  dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n_features) %>%
#  

print(boruta_features)

boruta_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("mo_ca ~", paste(boruta_features, collapse = " + "))
)
```

## Cross-validation folds

```{r}
reduced.cv.folds <-
  recipes::bake(reduced.recipe, new_data = training(reduced.split)) %>%
  rsample::group_vfold_cv(group = participant, v = 5)

filtered.cv.folds <-
  recipes::bake(filtered.recipe, new_data = training(filtered.split)) %>%
  rsample::group_vfold_cv(group = participant, v = 5)

clean.cv.folds <-
  recipes::bake(clean.recipe, new_data = training(clean.split)) %>%
  rsample::group_vfold_cv(group = participant, v = 5)
```

## Model specs & workflows

Each model gets three workflows:

- **Full** — all features, `filtered.formula` (the `filtered` pipeline).
- **Reduced** — `reduced.formula`, i.e. `reduced.data` after manually dropping highly-correlated
  variables (see Data inspection above). This is the feature set we compare against the SEM below.
- **Boruta** — `boruta_formula`, the Boruta-confirmed feature subset, always evaluated on the
  `filtered` pipeline since that's where Boruta was run.

### Catboost

```{r}
catboost_model <-
  parsnip::boost_tree(
    mode = "regression",
    trees = tune(),
    min_n = 5,
    learn_rate = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune()
  ) %>%
  set_engine("catboost", loss_function = "RMSE")

catboost_params <- dials::parameters(
  trees(range = c(50, 500)),
  tree_depth(range = c(4, 10)), # In most cases, optimal depth ranges 4-10; 6-10 recommended.
  learn_rate()
)

catboost.grid <- dials::grid_space_filling(catboost_params, size = 20)

catboost.workflow <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(catboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(filtered.formula) # Full model, filtered pipeline

catboost_reduced_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(catboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(reduced.formula) # Reduced model, correlation-reduced pipeline

catboost_boruta_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(catboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(boruta_formula) # Boruta-only model
```

### XGBoost

```{r}
xgboost_model <-
  parsnip::boost_tree(
    mode = "regression",
    trees = 1500,
    min_n = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune(),
    learn_rate = tune(),
    loss_reduction = tune()
  ) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost", objective = "reg:squarederror")

xgboost_params <- dials::parameters(min_n(), tree_depth(), learn_rate(), loss_reduction())
xgboost_grid <- dials::grid_space_filling(xgboost_params, size = 60)

xgboost_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(xgboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(filtered.formula) # Full model, filtered pipeline

xgboost_reduced_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(xgboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(reduced.formula) # Reduced model, correlation-reduced pipeline

xgboost_boruta_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(xgboost_model) %>%
  add_formula(boruta_formula) # Boruta-only model, filtered pipeline
```

### LightGBM

```{r}
lightgbm_model <-
  parsnip::boost_tree(
    mode = "regression",
    trees = 1000,
    min_n = tune(),
    tree_depth = tune()
  ) %>%
  set_engine("lightgbm", objective = "regression", verbose = -1)

lightgbm_params <- dials::parameters(min_n(), tree_depth())
lgbm_grid <- dials::grid_space_filling(lightgbm_params, size = 30)

lgbm_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(lightgbm_model) %>%
  add_formula(filtered.formula) # Full model, filtered pipeline

lgbm_reduced_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(lightgbm_model) %>%
  add_formula(reduced.formula) # Reduced model, correlation-reduced pipeline

lgbm_boruta_wf <-
  workflows::workflow() %>%
  add_model(lightgbm_model) %>%
  add_formula(boruta_formula) # Boruta-only model
```

# Training

All "Boruta" workflows are tuned against `filtered.cv.folds`, matching the pipeline the Boruta
features were derived from. The XGBoost "Full" workflow is tuned against `reduced.cv.folds` as a
separate baseline (kept from the original design); everything else uses `filtered.cv.folds`.

## Catboost

```{r}
filtered.catboost.tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = catboost.workflow,
  resamples = filtered.cv.folds,
  grid = catboost.grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

reduced.catboost.tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = catboost_reduced_wf,
  resamples = reduced.cv.folds,
  grid = catboost.grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

boruta.catboost.tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = catboost_boruta_wf,
  resamples = filtered.cv.folds,
  grid = catboost.grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

filtered.catboost.tuned %>% tune::show_best(metric = "rmse", n = 5)

filtered.catboost.tuned %>%
  tune::show_best(metric = "rmse", n = 10) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(trees:learn_rate, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, mean)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 1 / 2) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free") +
  ggtitle("CatBoost Full: best parameters for RMSE")
```

```{r}
filtered.train.processed <- bake(filtered.recipe, new_data = training(filtered.split))
reduced.train.processed  <- bake(reduced.recipe,  new_data = training(reduced.split))

cat_full_fit <- catboost.workflow %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(filtered.catboost.tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = filtered.train.processed)

cat_reduced_fit <- catboost_reduced_wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(reduced.catboost.tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = reduced.train.processed)

cat_boruta_fit <- catboost_boruta_wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(boruta.catboost.tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = filtered.train.processed)

saveRDS(cat_full_fit, "catboost_full_model.rds")
saveRDS(cat_reduced_fit, "catboost_reduced_model.rds")
saveRDS(cat_boruta_fit, "catboost_boruta_model.rds")
```

```{r}
# Feature importance comparison: Full vs Reduced vs Boruta
# NOTE: catboost.get_feature_importance() only returns scores for columns actually used as
# predictors by the fitted formula — id-role columns like `participant` are excluded by the recipe's
# formula even though they're still present in the baked data frame. Drop them here too, or the
# name/score vectors won't line up (this is what caused the earlier tibble() size-mismatch error).
cb_engine_full    <- extract_fit_engine(cat_full_fit)
cb_engine_reduced <- extract_fit_engine(cat_reduced_fit)
cb_engine_boruta  <- extract_fit_engine(cat_boruta_fit)

features_full    <- colnames(filtered.train.processed %>% select(-mo_ca, -participant))
features_reduced <- colnames(reduced.train.processed  %>% select(-mo_ca, -participant))
features_boruta  <- boruta_features

stopifnot(
  "CatBoost Full: feature/importance length mismatch" =
    length(features_full) == length(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_full)),
  "CatBoost Reduced: feature/importance length mismatch" =
    length(features_reduced) == length(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_reduced)),
  "CatBoost Boruta: feature/importance length mismatch" =
    length(features_boruta) == length(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_boruta))
)

cb_imp_full <- tibble(
  feature = features_full,
  importance = as.vector(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_full)),
  Model = "Full Model"
)

cb_imp_reduced <- tibble(
  feature = features_reduced,
  importance = as.vector(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_reduced)),
  Model = "Reduced Model"
)

cb_imp_boruta <- tibble(
  feature = features_boruta,
  importance = as.vector(catboost.get_feature_importance(cb_engine_boruta)),
  Model = "Boruta Model"
)

bind_rows(cb_imp_full, cb_imp_reduced, cb_imp_boruta) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  slice_max(importance, n = 10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(feature, importance), y = importance, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Model, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Full Model" = "#3498db", "Reduced Model" = "#e67e22", "Boruta Model" = "#2ecc71")) +
  labs(title = "CatBoost Feature Importance Comparison", x = NULL, y = "Importance Score")
```

## XGBoost

```{r}
train_processed_reduced  <- bake(reduced.recipe, new_data = training(reduced.split))
train_processed_filtered <- bake(filtered.recipe, new_data = training(filtered.split))

xgboost_tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = xgboost_wf,
  resamples = filtered.cv.folds,
  grid = xgboost_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

xgboost_reduced_tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = xgboost_reduced_wf,
  resamples = reduced.cv.folds,
  grid = xgboost_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

xgboost_boruta_tuned <- tune::tune_grid(
  object = xgboost_boruta_wf,
  resamples = filtered.cv.folds,
  grid = xgboost_grid,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(rmse, rsq, mae),
  control = tune::control_grid(verbose = TRUE)
)

xgboost_tuned %>% tune::show_best(metric = "rmse") %>% knitr::kable()

xgb_full_fit <- xgboost_wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(xgboost_tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = train_processed_filtered)

xgb_reduced_fit <- xgboost_reduced_wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(xgboost_reduced_tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = train_processed_reduced)

xgb_boruta_fit <- xgboost_boruta_wf %>%
  finalize_workflow(select_best(xgboost_boruta_tuned, metric = "rmse")) %>%
  fit(data = train_processed_filtered)

saveRDS(xgb_full_fit, "xgboost_full_model.rds")
saveRDS(xgb_reduced_fit, "xgboost_reduced_model.rds")
saveRDS(xgb_boruta_fit, "xgboost_boruta_model.rds")
```

```{r}
xgb_engine_full    <- extract_fit_engine(xgb_full_fit)
xgb_engine_reduced <- extract_fit_engine(xgb_reduced_fit)
xgb_engine_boruta  <- extract_fit_engine(xgb_boruta_fit)

xgb_imp_full <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_engine_full) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Full Model")

xgb_imp_reduced <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_engine_reduced) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Reduced Model")

xgb_imp_boruta <- xgb.importance(model = xgb_engine_boruta) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Boruta Model")

bind_rows(xgb_imp_full, xgb_imp_reduced, xgb_imp_boruta) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  slice_max(Importance, n = 10) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Model, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Full Model" = "#3498db", "Reduced Model" = "#e67e22", "Boruta Model" = "#2ecc71")) +
  labs(title = "XGBoost Feature Importance Comparison", x = NULL, y = "Importance Score (Gain)")
```

```{r}

lgbm_imp_full <- lgb.importance(lgbm_engine_full) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Full Model")

lgbm_imp_reduced <- lgb.importance(lgbm_engine_reduced) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Reduced Model")

lgbm_imp_boruta <- lgb.importance(lgbm_engine_boruta) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(Variable = Feature, Importance = Gain) %>%
  mutate(Model = "Boruta Model")

bind_rows(lgbm_imp_full, lgbm_imp_reduced, lgbm_imp_boruta) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  slice_max(Importance, n = 10) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Model, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Full Model" = "#3498db", "Reduced Model" = "#e67e22", "Boruta Model" = "#2ecc71")) +
  labs(title = "LightGBM Feature Importance Comparison", x = NULL, y = "Importance Score (Gain)")
```

## Cross-validation RMSE comparison

```{r}
comparison_results <- bind_rows(
  show_best(filtered.catboost.tuned, metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Full"),
  show_best(reduced.catboost.tuned,  metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Reduced"),
  show_best(boruta.catboost.tuned,   metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Boruta"),
  show_best(xgboost_tuned,           metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Full"),
  show_best(xgboost_reduced_tuned,   metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Reduced"),
  show_best(xgboost_boruta_tuned,    metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Boruta"),
  show_best(lgbm_tuned,              metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Full"),
  show_best(lgbm_reduced_tuned,      metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Reduced"),
  show_best(lgbm_boruta_tuned,       metric = "rmse", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Boruta")
) %>%
  select(model, mean, std_err) %>%
  arrange(mean)

knitr::kable(comparison_results, caption = "Cross-Validation RMSE Comparison (Full vs. Reduced vs. Boruta)")
```

# Test

All models below are evaluated on their **held-out test sets**, using the finalized fits from the
Training section above (`*_full_fit`, `*_reduced_fit`, `*_boruta_fit` for each of CatBoost, XGBoost,
LightGBM) — not refit on training data again.

```{r}
test_processed_filtered <- bake(filtered.recipe, new_data = testing(filtered.split))
test_processed_reduced  <- bake(reduced.recipe,  new_data = testing(reduced.split))

preds_cat_full     <- predict(cat_full_fit,     test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Full")
preds_cat_reduced  <- predict(cat_reduced_fit,  test_processed_reduced)  %>% bind_cols(testing(reduced.split))  %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Reduced")
preds_cat_boruta   <- predict(cat_boruta_fit,   test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "CatBoost Boruta")
preds_xgb_full     <- predict(xgb_full_fit,     test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Full")
preds_xgb_reduced  <- predict(xgb_reduced_fit,  test_processed_reduced)  %>% bind_cols(testing(reduced.split))  %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Reduced")
preds_xgb_boruta   <- predict(xgb_boruta_fit,   test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost Boruta")
preds_lgbm_full    <- predict(lgbm_full_fit,    test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Full")
preds_lgbm_reduced <- predict(lgbm_reduced_fit, test_processed_reduced)  %>% bind_cols(testing(reduced.split))  %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Reduced")
preds_lgbm_boruta  <- predict(lgbm_boruta_fit,  test_processed_filtered) %>% bind_cols(testing(filtered.split)) %>% mutate(model = "LightGBM Boruta")

all_predictions <- bind_rows(
  preds_cat_full, preds_cat_reduced, preds_cat_boruta,
  preds_xgb_full, preds_xgb_reduced, preds_xgb_boruta,
  preds_lgbm_full, preds_lgbm_reduced, preds_lgbm_boruta
)

# Test-set accuracy metrics (RMSE, RSQ, MAE)
test_metrics <- all_predictions %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  yardstick::metrics(truth = mo_ca, estimate = .pred) %>%
  select(model, .metric, .estimate) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = .metric, values_from = .estimate) %>%
  arrange(rmse)

knitr::kable(test_metrics, digits = 3, caption = "Final Test Set Metrics: Full vs Reduced vs Boruta Models")

# Residual diagnostics
all_predictions %>%
  mutate(residual_pct = (mo_ca - .pred) / .pred,
         feature_set = case_when(
           grepl("Boruta", model) ~ "Boruta",
           grepl("Reduced", model) ~ "Reduced",
           TRUE ~ "Full"
         )) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = .pred, y = residual_pct, color = feature_set)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Full" = "#3498db", "Reduced" = "#e67e22", "Boruta" = "#2ecc71")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Test Set Residual Diagnostics",
    subtitle = "Comparing Full vs Reduced vs Boruta Features across Models",
    x = "Predicted MoCa Score",
    y = "Residual (%)",
    color = "Feature set"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)


```

# SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations)

Explaining the **Boruta-selected XGBoost model** (`xgb_boruta_fit`), since that's the model we
actually care about interpreting — restricted to the Boruta feature set.

```{r}
X_explain <- testing(filtered.split)[, boruta_features]

# 1.5 minutes on laptop
# Note: if you have more than p=8 features, use kernelshap() instead of permshap()
system.time(
  shap_values <- xgb_boruta_fit |>
    permshap(X = X_explain, feature_names = boruta_features, exact = FALSE) |>
    shapviz()
)

saveRDS(shap_values, file = "shap_values.rds")
shap_values <- readRDS("shap_values.rds")

shap_values |> sv_importance("bee", max_display = 15, size = 0.5)
shap_values |> sv_importance(kind = "both", show_numbers = TRUE)

# Dependence plots for the top Boruta features (adjust to taste / to match your actual
# boruta_features — this list must be a subset of boruta_features)
dependence_vars <- intersect(
  c("interviewer", "l_mean", "ba", "physical_activity", "sleep", "aid_strength_left"),
  boruta_features
)
shap_values |> sv_dependence(dependence_vars, color_var = "auto")

shap_values |> sv_force(row_id = 5)
shap_values |> sv_waterfall(row_id = 40)
```

# SEM on full data (comparison to Reduced ML models)

The tree ensembles above needed the manual correlation-based feature pruning (`reduced.data`)
because highly collinear predictors hurt split-based models. A multilevel SEM handles that
collinearity through its latent-variable structure instead, so here it's run on the **full**,
un-pruned feature set — giving us a like-for-like comparison against the "Reduced" ML models above
without needing to drop any variables by hand first.

> **Important:** the model below uses raw column names (`PerformanceLog`, `MoCa`, `Gender`,
> `R_variation`, `STE`, etc.) as they appear *before* the `janitor::clean_names()` step used
> elsewhere in this script — because that step lowercases/renames everything and also drops some of
> the demographic columns this model needs (`Gender`, `Handedness`, `Age`, `Educational_level`) in
> favor of derived 0/1 dummies. `sem.data` below is built straight from `clean.raw` to preserve the
> original names. **Double-check these names against your actual `clean.RDS` columns** — if any
> don't match, adjust the `paste0()` string accordingly rather than the upstream data pipeline.

```{r}
# Full (un-reduced) feature set with original column names preserved, for SEM
sem.data <- clean.raw %>%
  select(all_of(cols_to_use)) %>%
  filter(Task == "training")

# --- Diagnostic: filter(Task == "training") is the most likely reason EVERY variable would get
# flagged at once (n_non_na = 0 for all columns if this returns zero rows) — check that before
# looking anywhere else.
message("Distinct raw Task values (with counts):")
print(table(clean.raw$Task, useNA = "always"))
message("Rows in sem.data after filtering to Task == 'training': ", nrow(sem.data))

if (nrow(sem.data) == 0) {
  # Fall back to a case/whitespace-insensitive match instead of guessing the exact literal string
  sem.data <- clean.raw %>%
    select(all_of(cols_to_use)) %>%
    filter(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_trim(Task)) == "training")
  message("Retried with case/whitespace-insensitive match — rows now: ", nrow(sem.data))
}

sem.data <- sem.data %>%
  mutate(
    Gender = case_when(Gender == "Male" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0),
    Handedness = case_when(Handedness == "Right handed" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  )

# --- Diagnostic: check every variable the SEM model actually uses BEFORE fitting, so a bad
# column (constant, all-NA, still non-numeric, etc.) is reported clearly here instead of via
# lavaan's generic "no finite variance" / "missing observed variables" errors.
sem_vars <- c(
  "Participant", "PerformanceLog", "MoCA",
  "mean_blink_count", "average_blink_duration", "mean_saccadic_count", "average_saccadic_duration",
  "mean_fixation_count", "average_fixation_duration", "R_variation", "R_entropy", "R_mean",
  "gaze_entropy", "STE", "GTE", "BA",
  "Age", "Gender", "Depression", "Anxiety", "Stress", "Sleep", "Walking",
  "Physical_activity", "Handedness", "Snellen_left"
)

sem_var_diag <- purrr::map_dfr(sem_vars, function(v) {
  if (!v %in% names(sem.data)) {
    return(tibble(variable = v, present = FALSE, class = NA_character_,
                   n_non_na = NA_integer_, n_distinct = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_))
  }
  x <- sem.data[[v]]
  tibble(
    variable = v,
    present = TRUE,
    class = class(x)[1],
    n_non_na = sum(!is.na(x)),
    n_distinct = dplyr::n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = if (is.numeric(x)) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
  )
})

problem_vars <- sem_var_diag %>%
  filter(!present | n_distinct <= 1 | n_non_na <= 1 | is.na(sd) | sd == 0 | class %in% c("character", "factor"))

print(sem_var_diag, n = Inf)
if (nrow(problem_vars) > 0) {
  warning("SEM variables likely to break lavaan (constant / all-NA / non-numeric): ",
          paste(problem_vars$variable, collapse = ", "))
}
# --- END CHANGED

# Define the SEM model
model <- paste0('
# Within cluster performance across tasks for 1 participant
level: 1
    #Measured by
    L1.SPACE =~ PerformanceLog
    #Regressed on
    L1.SPACE ~ mean_blink_count + average_blink_duration + mean_saccadic_count + average_saccadic_duration + mean_fixation_count + average_fixation_duration + R_variation + R_entropy + R_mean + gaze_entropy + STE + GTE + BA
# Between Cognitive ability (MoCA) predicted by physiological + demographic factors
level: 2
    #Measured by
    L2 =~ MoCA
    L1.SPACE =~ PerformanceLog
    #Regressed on
    L2 ~  L1.SPACE + Age + Gender + Depression + Anxiety + Stress  + Sleep + Walking + Physical_activity + Handedness + Snellen_left
    L1.SPACE ~ mean_blink_count + average_blink_duration + mean_saccadic_count + average_saccadic_duration + mean_fixation_count + average_fixation_duration + R_variation + R_entropy + R_mean + gaze_entropy + STE + GTE + BA
')

# Fit the SEM
fit <- sem(model, data = sem.data, std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml", cluster = "Participant")

# Summarize results
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
lavInspect(fit, "icc")
lavInspect(fit, "h1")
varTable(fit)
lavaanPlot(fit)

test_layout <- t(get_layout(fit))
graph_sem(
  model = fit,
  layout = test_layout,
  rect_width = 0.2,
  rect_height = 0.2,
  text_size = 2
)
```

## Inspectthe model

```{r}
lavInspect(fit, "converged")
lavInspect(fit, "post.check")          # flags Heywood cases / negative variances
summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)      # look for warnings printed above the table
fitmeasures(fit, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))
semPlot::semPaths(fit, what = "std", layout = "tree",
                   whatLabels = "std", edge.label.cex = 0.6,
                   rotation = 2, nCharNodes = 0)
```

Note these aren't directly comparable numbers — the ML "Reduced" models predict `mo_ca` in a single
step from a feature-pruned set, while the SEM decomposes variance across two nested levels
(within-participant `PerformanceLog` and between-participant `MoCa`) using the full feature set. The
tables above are meant to be read side by side rather than merged into one ranking: the SEM's `MoCa`
R\u00b2 is the more apples-to-apples number against the Reduced ML models' `rsq`.
